answer: An agent economy can require a self-prediction bond before every trade: each agent stakes a small pearl of its own funds, betting its trade will pass a peer audit, like a toll paid to cross a bridge that is refunded only on the far side. One honest agent risks one pearl per trade and wins it back. A sybil farmer must stake a pearl for every fake trade, and each failed audit burns the bond, so the old fable that fake volume is free collapses: a thousand fakes pay a thousand bonds, each checked by strangers.
